name: Pantsir-S1

cost.display: ~$13–15M per unit on the export market

key_facts.label: Armament
key_facts.value: 12 SAMs + twin 30mm autocannons on one chassis

key_facts.label: Role
key_facts.value: Point defense for high-value sites and maneuver units

short_role: Combined gun-and-missile point-defense system protecting high-value sites and forward units from aircraft, missiles and drones.
characteristics: 12 ready-to-fire short-range SAMs plus twin 30mm autocannons on a single vehicle
Radar and optical tracking for engagement at multiple altitudes and speeds
A high-value, expensive-per-unit system that has itself become a target for cheap strike drones
Several units reportedly lost to drone strikes at a small fraction of the Pantsir's own unit cost
employment_notes: Deployed to protect specific high-value sites and forward troop concentrations rather than blanket the whole line — its own cost and relative scarcity mean it is positioned selectively, and losing one to a strike drone costing a tiny fraction of its price is a stark illustration of the cost-asymmetry running through this whole battlefield.
contrast_vs_traditional: A premium multi-million-dollar point-defense system was designed against aircraft and cruise missiles, the threats it remains genuinely effective against. It is considerably less cost-efficient against the mass cheap-drone threat that now accounts for 60–70% of equipment losses on this battlefield — the same asymmetry problem Western Patriot batteries and Gepard guns face from the other direction, just with different unit economics on this side.

sources.label: Forbes — APKWS And Pantsir-S1s: Saudi Arabia Acquiring More Cost-Effective Defenses Against Drones
